intro: This branch teaches calculating with fractions: adding, subtracting, multiplying and simple dividing. The key idea is that fractions can only be added or subtracted when the parts are the same size.

II.6.01.what: Adding fractions that have the same bottom number (denominator), so the parts are the same size.

levels.a: Adds fractions using a picture of a fraction bar.
levels.b: Adds them with numbers alone, adding the tops and keeping the bottom.
levels.c: Adds fractions whose total is more than 1, writing it as a mixed number.
levels.d: Solves story problems, like how much pizza two people ate.

II.6.02.what: Subtracting fractions that have the same bottom number.

levels.a: Subtracts fractions by crossing out parts in a picture.
levels.c: Subtracts a fraction from one whole.
levels.d: Solves story problems, like how much cake is left.

II.6.03.what: Splitting a fraction into smaller fractions that add up to it, as a tool for adding.

levels.a: Writes three quarters as one quarter plus one quarter plus one quarter.
levels.b: Finds several different ways to split the same fraction.
levels.c: Splits an improper fraction into wholes plus a fraction.
levels.d: Splits one fraction to make a whole first, which makes adding easier.
levels.e: Finds the missing fraction with 1 on top that completes a sum, like one third plus one over what.
levels.f: Splits a fraction with 1 on top into two different such fractions, finding the largest bottom possible.

II.6.04.what: Adding and subtracting mixed numbers (a whole number plus a fraction) with the same bottom number.

levels.a: Adds the wholes and the fraction parts separately.
levels.b: Swaps one whole for its fraction pieces, so five and a fifth becomes four and six fifths.
levels.c: Subtracts mixed numbers when a whole must be broken up first.
levels.d: Solves story problems, like total distance walked over two days.

II.6.05.what: Rewriting two fractions so they have the same bottom number (a common denominator), which is needed before adding them.

levels.a: Finds the smallest common bottom number using least common multiples.
levels.b: Uses the two bottom numbers multiplied together as a common bottom number.
levels.c: Rewrites a fraction with a new, larger bottom number.
levels.d: Chooses the smallest common bottom number from several options.

II.6.06.what: Adding fractions with different bottom numbers by first making the parts the same size.

levels.a: Adds using fraction strips cut into matching pieces.
levels.b: Rewrites both fractions with a common bottom number, then adds.
levels.c: Gives the answer in simplest form.
levels.d: Adds three fractions with different bottom numbers.
levels.e: Finds the missing top number in a sum of fractions with different bottoms.
levels.f: Adds a long chain of fractions using a trick where almost every piece cancels out.

II.6.07.what: Subtracting fractions with different bottom numbers.

levels.a: Subtracts using fraction strips cut into matching pieces.
levels.b: Rewrites both fractions with a common bottom number, then subtracts.
levels.c: Gives the answer in simplest form.
levels.d: Solves story problems, like how much pizza is left.

II.6.08.what: Adding and subtracting mixed numbers whose fraction parts have different bottom numbers.

levels.c: Handles fraction parts that add to more than a whole, or need a whole broken up.
levels.d: Estimates the answer first by rounding to whole numbers.

II.6.09.what: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number, like 3 lots of two fifths.

levels.a: Writes it as a repeated addition of the fraction.
levels.b: Multiplies the top by the whole number, keeping the bottom.
levels.c: Shows it as equal jumps along a number line.
levels.d: Solves word problems, like the total length of several equal pieces of string.

II.6.10.what: Multiplying one fraction by another, which finds a fraction of a fraction.

levels.a: Uses an overlapping-rectangle picture to find the answer.
levels.b: Multiplies the tops together and the bottoms together.
levels.c: Simplifies before multiplying to keep the numbers small.
levels.e: Finds the missing top number that makes a fraction product come out right.
levels.f: Multiplies a long chain of fractions where each top cancels the bottom next to it.

II.6.11.what: Understanding multiplication as resizing: multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes a number smaller, and more than 1 makes it bigger.

levels.a: Predicts that multiplying by a fraction less than 1 shrinks a number.
levels.b: Predicts that multiplying by a fraction more than 1 grows a number.
levels.c: Compares two such products without working them out.
levels.d: Judges and explains statements about whether a product grows or shrinks.

II.6.12.what: Dividing a unit fraction (one part, like one half) by a whole number, like sharing half a liter among 5 cups.

levels.a: Splits a shaded part of a bar into equal pieces and names each piece.
levels.b: Divides with numbers alone, as in one third divided by 5 is one fifteenth.
levels.d: Checks an answer by multiplying back.

II.6.13.what: Dividing a whole number by a unit fraction, which asks how many of those parts fit into it.

levels.a: Counts the fraction pieces in whole bars to find the answer.
levels.b: Works out how many sevenths fit into 3, and similar.
levels.c: Solves story problems, like how many children can have a fifth of a pizza each.
levels.d: Checks an answer by multiplying back.

II.6.14.what: Solving word problems that involve calculating with fractions.

levels.a: Chooses which operation a fraction problem needs.
levels.b: Solves problems that take more than one step.
levels.c: Solves problems that involve mixed numbers, like scaling up a recipe.
levels.d: Judges whether an answer is reasonable by estimating.
levels.e: Works backwards: from how much a fraction change took, finds the whole amount.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: from a bottle's full and part-full weights, finds the empty bottle's weight.
